REVIEW NOTE: almost every citation below was re-opened and checks out. Corrections are marked [fixed].

WHAT THE LYRICS SCREEN DOES TODAY (inventory)
On screen (App/Features/Lyrics/LyricsView.swift):
- Animated artwork background, drawn by a SwiftUI ShaderLibrary shader in a TimelineView (LyricsArtworkBackground.swift:49, 86), so glass can sample it. A black scrim sits behind the controls (LyricsView.swift:124-129, 0 to 38 %).
- Karaoke lines with tap-to-seek, drag/fling and snap-back; or plain lyrics; or the loading / no-lyrics state (LyricsView.swift:232-262). The no-lyrics state shows InstrumentalRenderAction (Render / Play instrumental, Find or import lyrics) and "Add lyrics and sync them" (LyricsStaticContent.swift:196-217).
- A track pill on top (LyricsChrome.swift:71-104), plus the "Make the words light up · Sync it yourself" chip when the lyrics have no word timing (LyricsView.swift:82-85, 297-300; LyricsChrome.swift:486-518).
- Bottom cluster (LyricsChrome.swift:175-212): an optional sync-offset row (±0.5 s / ±0.1 s / reset), play/pause, the wavy seek bar that previews lyrics while dragging, then the toolbar Back · Synced · Static · More (LyricsChrome.swift:350-392). The segments are at 363-373. "Synced" is disabled when there is no synced text.
- [fixed] With no lyrics (showSyncedLyrics == nil) only the two segments become a spacer (372); Back and More stay. The toolbar is not hidden.
- A floating instrumental toggle above the cluster, only when a render exists (LyricsView.swift:312). [fixed path] App/Features/Tais/InstrumentalLyricsViews.swift:94-133, id lyrics.instrumentalToggle; no test uses that id.
- Immersive mode auto-hides the controls, and a "show controls" disc brings them back (LyricsView.swift:87-89, 137-142, 473-488).
- Swipe sideways for previous / next track (LyricsView.swift:490-509) and a toast (LyricsView.swift:157-167, 582-594).
- Fetch dialog: search online (auto-apply or pick), manual title/artist, import a file (FetchLyricsDialog.swift).
- Save Lyrics alert with .lrc export (LyricsView.swift:200-218) and on-device translation via translationTask (LyricsView.swift:219-226, 418-445).

How synced vs plain is chosen today (showSyncedLyrics, LyricsView.swift:62-72): synced when it exists, else plain. The segment only sets syncedOverride/overrideSongId (334-338), which resets on song change (179).

More sheet (LyricsMoreSheet.swift):
- Lyrics group (82-119): Sync the words yourself / Fix my word timing, Save Lyrics, Translate via AI, Translate on device, Reset imported lyrics, Lyrics debug info.
- Appearance (121-138): alignment left / center / right.

There is also no "re-search / change lyrics" action once lyrics exist; you have to reset first.
- The route-level copy, LyricsOptionsSheet (LyricsView.swift:618-646), reuses the same view without the screen-only actions. It is presented with the default .pixlSheet() [.medium, .large] (App/Shell/RouteDestinations.swift:53). [new] So the Keep screen on row shows there too.

KEEP SCREEN ON: every reference (grep-verified, none elsewhere in App/, AppTests/ or UITests/)
- LyricsViewPreferences.swift:5-7 (doc), 12 (keepScreenOnKey = "keep_screen_on_lyrics"), 22 (property), 29 (init, default false).

Exports only write stored keys of kind .portable (SettingsBackup.swift:193-199). The clear step only clears portable keys (267). An android-only key on restore is skipped and reported (PreferencesModule.swift:236-260).

LyricsSyncEditorView.open swaps router.cover (LyricsSyncEditorView.swift:38-42; Router.swift:84-86), and onClosed swaps it back (185-187). One screen's onDisappear (false) could land after the other's onAppear (true). This ordering is plausible but not proven from code.

EVIDENCE FROM CI SCREENSHOTS [new]
Source: run 37142339689, artifact shots-c7dee2d…, the latest main.
- lyricsWordFill-dark / lyricsBrightArt-dark: the chrome does render as glass (rims and specular edges on the pill, seek bar, circles and segments). But the panels read as dark, flat plastic, and play/pause and the active Synced segment read as solid paint.
- lyricsMoreSheet-dark: a full-height, opaque, near-black sheet with no visible glass at all.
- lyricsOptions-dark: the same LyricsMoreSheet at the default medium detent. It shows as an inset Liquid Glass sheet with the content behind reading through the fills.

2026-10-03 always-dark change (fe07132, docs in 3a9e20f, verified):
- It only switched the palette source to themeStore.colors(for: .dark) and swapped preferredColorScheme(.dark) for alwaysDarkTheme (Theme.swift).
- It added playerTheme and preferredColorScheme to the More sheet (LyricsView.swift:384-386), and did the same in LyricsSyncEditorView.
- `git show fe07132` contains no glassEffect or presentationBackground change. It did NOT remove glass.
rootCause:
"Zero Liquid Glass" has two parts, and the CI screenshots now back both. Which one Hoa means is ambiguous; see owner decision 1.

(A) The More sheet, where the Keep screen on switch lives, literally has no glass.
- It is presented only at .large (LyricsView.swift:387).
- WWDC25-323: on iOS 26 a full-height sheet's glass "gradually transitions, becoming opaque and anchoring to the edge of the screen".
- lyricsMoreSheet-dark shows an opaque sheet. The same view at the default [.medium, .large] (lyricsOptions-dark, RouteDestinations.swift:53) is visibly glass.
- Hoa's sentence ties "remove the toggle" to "that page has 0 liquid glass", and the toggle is on this sheet. So this is probably the main complaint.

(B) The lyrics screen's chrome is glass, but it reads as solid.
1. The panels are tinted with a dark album role, about 34 % (LyricsChrome.swift:40-42), over the dark graded background. The full player's owner-approved top buttons use a 14 % onPrimary breath (GlassTint.playerChrome).
2. Play/pause (232), the active segment (418) and the discs (480, 537) are at GlassTint.prominent 0.85. That matches the full player's transport, so it's consistent, but it reads as paint.
3. The glass never has anything with edges behind it. The karaoke mask clears every lyric line above the header inset and below the controls (KaraokeLyricsView.swift:133-137; LyricsEdgeFade.resolve in Packages/PixlCore/Sources/PixlLyrics/Engine/LyricsRenderMath.swift:395-411). Behind the bottom bar there is also a 38 % black scrim (LyricsView.swift:124-129).
4. No GlassEffectContainer exists in Features/Lyrics, so nothing merges or morphs. The Synced/Static switch only animates a corner radius.
5. The seek bar is a control without .interactive(). [fixed] The track pill is not a control, so it should stay non-interactive.
6. The fetch dialog dims the screen 45 % and tints its card 62 %, with fills inside.

Alternative causes on the phone (unverified, ask Hoa):
- Settings › Display & Brightness › Liquid Glass set to "Tinted" (iOS 26.1+), or Reduce Transparency / Increase Contrast, makes all glass more frosted. Under Increase Contrast the lyrics container also jumps to 0.92 (LyricsChrome.swift:23).
- These would affect the whole app, though, and Hoa only singles out this page.

Separate bug found on the way (verified; overlaps owner item 7, the heart button):
- LibraryStore.songsById is @ObservationIgnored (App/Stores/LibraryStore.swift:25). LibraryStore.song(id:) reads only that (50), and applyEdit patches it (111-119). So LibraryEditor.isFavorite (App/Features/Library/LibraryEditing.swift:108) registers no observation.
- The More sheet's heart (LyricsView.swift:368, 636 → LyricsMoreSheet.swift:176) only refreshes when something tracked changes, such as tapping shuffle or repeat.
- The full player's PlayerToggleRow gets isFavorite the same way (NowPlayingView.swift:110-114).

options.name: A. Translate · Sing (two segments, recommended)
options.description:
The two 50 pt segments become two independent toggles inside the cluster's single GlassEffectContainer.

TRANSLATE
- Active means translations are showing.
- Tap when the lyrics already have translations: toggles preferences.showTranslation.
- Tap otherwise: runs the existing on-device Translation flow (LyricsView.startTranslation, LyricsView.swift:418-445) and turns translations on.
- Long-press .contextMenu: Translate via AI, plus Show romanization when controller.hasRomanizedLyrics.

SING
- Karaoke mode: the existing MDX-Net instrumental with its in-sync 700 ms crossfade (App/Services/ML/InstrumentalController.swift).
- With a render (env.tais.instrumental.isAvailable): toggles vocals off/on (toggle(), :66). Active means 'Vocals off'.
- Without a render: starts env.tais.studio.start(.instrumental, song:) and shows 'Removing vocals NN %' as a fill inside the glass.
- It's per song: a new song starts with vocals, as the controller resets isActive (InstrumentalController.swift:45-49).
- This replaces the floating InstrumentalLyricsToggle (LyricsView.swift:312).
options.pros: Translate is the most useful everyday action for a multilingual listener, and it's always relevant when lyrics exist. Sing is the flashiest thing the app can already do, and it belongs on a lyrics page. Both reuse finished engines, so the work is S-M. It keeps Android's two-segment geometry and the existing LyricsToggleSegment active/inactive morph. Removing the floating toggle declutters the screen.
options.cons:
- Sing needs the ~33 MB MDX model download and minutes of on-device work the first time.
- It fails on songs with no audio source (Spotify-only items; App/Services/ML/TaisServices.swift:35-58). Streamed YouTube songs are downloaded first.
- It does nothing audible while Spotify Connect drives playback, so disable it when playback.remoteOutputName != nil.
- On-device translation currently needs synced lines (startTranslation guard, LyricsView.swift:423), and applyTranslations only writes synced lines (App/Services/LyricsController.swift:263-264). Plain-only lyrics either disable Translate or need a small extension.
- It diverges from Android's FloatingInstrumentalToggle (owner override; update parity rows 25 and 27).

options.name: B. Translate · Light up words (AI word sync)
options.description: Translate as in A. The second segment runs the on-device Wav2Vec2 lyric sync (env.tais.studio.start(.lyrics, song:), as TaisStudioProgressCard.startLyrics does at TaisStudioProgressCard.swift:89-99, including the 'Replace your timing?' alert at 67-71). It turns line-synced or plain lyrics into word-by-word karaoke, with progress in the segment. When the lyrics are already word-timed, the slot becomes 'Adjust sync' (it shows or hides the offset row).
options.pros: Directly makes the karaoke view's best effect, word fill, available on more songs. It also fixes a parity gap: Android has this in its More sheet.
options.cons: Only useful on songs without word timing. Once BiniLyrics or user sync supplies word timing, the slot falls back to a less exciting action. It needs the alignment model download (~188 MB per TaisDemo).

options.name: C. Translate · Change lyrics (re-match)
options.description: The second segment opens the fetch dialog in pick mode (controller.searchOnline(song:forcePick: true), LyricsController.swift:128), so the listener can swap a wrong or line-only match for another catalog result (BiniLyrics, LRCLIB, AMLL, NetEase), with the source shown on the segment ('Lyrics: BiniLyrics').
options.pros: Fixes the most common real annoyance, a wrong or worse match. iOS has no way to do this today without resetting first. S effort.
options.cons: Not flashy. It's a fix-it action you use occasionally, not a toggle you play with.

options.name: D. Share lyric card
options.description: A Share segment: select 1-4 lines, render a card (the art-derived gradient background, the lines in SF Pro, title and artist) with ImageRenderer, and hand it to ShareLink.
options.pros: Very flashy and social. Something like it exists in big streaming apps.
options.cons: A brand-new feature: line-selection UI, a renderer and new API-ledger entries. L effort. Better as a More-sheet item or a later addition than as the main replacement.

- WWDC25 session 323, 'Build a SwiftUI app with the new design' (https://developer.apple.com/videos/play/wwdc2025/323/), verified quotes:
  - Sheets: "On iOS 26, partial height sheets are inset by default with a Liquid Glass background… When transitioning to a full height sheet, the glass background gradually transitions, becoming opaque and anchoring to the edge of the screen." Also: "If you've used the presentationBackground modifier… consider removing that".
  - Grouping: "glass can not sample other glass, so having nearby glass elements in different containers will result in inconsistent behavior. Using a glass container allows these elements to share their sampling region". This is why there is one container per cluster, and why glass rows on a glass sheet are optional.
  - Interaction: "for custom controls or for containers with interactive elements, add the interactive modifier… Glass reacts to user interaction by scaling, bouncing, and shimmering".
- 'Applying Liquid Glass to custom views' (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/applying-liquid-glass-to-custom-views), verified:
  - "Assign a tint color to suggest prominence."
  - "Apply the glassEffect(_:in:) modifier after other modifiers that affect the appearance of the view". This is why the .opacity at LyricsChrome.swift:421 should move.
  - Container spacing larger than the layout spacing "causes Liquid Glass effects to blend together at rest".
  - "Creating too many Liquid Glass effect containers… can degrade performance."
  - Default transition within spacing is matchedGeometry; "use the materialize transition and withAnimation(_:_:)… for effects… farther from each other than the container's assigned spacing".
- glassEffectTransition(_:) docs (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/view/glasseffecttransition(_:)): used "with the glassEffect(_:in:) view modifier and GlassEffectContainer view". So it is dropped from the container-less fetch dialog.
- Glass.clear (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/swiftui/glass/clear, iOS 26.0): "When using clear glass, ensure content remains legible by adding a dimming layer or other treatment beneath the glass." This supports keeping the 35 % black over bright art and the soft scrim.
- UIApplication.isIdleTimerDisabled (https://developer.apple.com/documentation/uikit/uiapplication/isidletimerdisabled, iOS 2.0): "You should set this property only if necessary and should be sure to reset it to false when the need no longer exists… This includes audio apps." The docs say nothing about background behaviour.
  - Developer reports that the flag can be reset when the app is backgrounded or killed (e.g. https://developer.apple.com/forums/thread/124483, and search results) are thin evidence, but enough to justify re-asserting on scenePhase .active.
  - [fixed] The original claim that 'iOS ignores the flag in the background, no scenePhase handling needed' is unsupported.
- iOS 26.1 added Settings › Display & Brightness › Liquid Glass: Clear / Tinted; Tinted makes glass more frosted (https://www.macworld.com/article/2947565/ios-26-1-beta-4-does-the-unthinkable-you-can-control-how-glassy-liquid-glass-should-be.html, https://www.tomsguide.com/phones/iphones/ios-26-1-lets-you-adjust-liquid-glass-transparency-on-your-iphone-heres-how-to-do-it). This is a possible device-side contributor.
